note: Lake Paho, a 273-acre MDC lake west of Princeton, has three small primitive campgrounds with privies. This entry is the "C" Campground on the peninsula just south of Route 145 where it crosses the lake's north end: gravel pull-offs among scattered trees off a gravel lane, open lake on both sides. Camping is only in the mapped campgrounds, with at most two camping units per site. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: page 'Individual Campsites', Rule 140 standard; brochure (2/2026) 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map'; map (11/2/2022) shows campgrounds B, C and D. Stored pin = GIS 233 = 'C' Campground (gravel pull-offs on the peninsula south of Rt 145). Lakeview held (pads ~42-60 m from the east shore over open grass; lakefront lead flagged). Split proposed for 'B' Campground (1.40 km SE, own road off Rt 145). Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights now manual. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION: area page 'Things to Do When You Visit: Camping: Individual Campsites'; Rule 140 standard, no special-use-permit-only rule. Brochure (2/2026): 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map. Camping is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period. ... Groups of 10 campers or more must obtain a special use permit. Campground quiet hours are in effect from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. All non-campers must leave by 10 p.m. Only two camping or sleeping units (car, van, motor home, pickup truck, tent or travel trailer) are permitted at each site. Camping rules are posted in each campground.' Map (11/2/2022): 'B' Campground, 'C' Campground and 'D' Campground, each with a Primitive Camping symbol, parking lot and privy.

CLUSTERS (three campgrounds, measured from site centres): 'C' = GIS 233 = stored pin, on the peninsula immediately south of Route 145 at the lake's north narrows (entrance: a gravel lane south off Rt 145; lot 2213 and a shelter/privy at its south end). 'D' = GIS 234 (40.41423,-93.66769), a small gravel turnaround loop on the north shore of the west arm, 410 m SW of C, reached by the gravel road MDC labels 'UNKNOWN' off Rt 145 west of C - too close for a split. 'B' = GIS 235 (40.40796,-93.65686), on the peninsula on the lake's east side: a gravel lane with about ten gravel back-in spurs ending at a turnaround with a privy (lot 3007, 40.40596,-93.65805); its own MDC improved road leaves Rt 145 at about 40.4096,-93.6551, about 1 km SE of C's entrance.

SPLIT PROPOSAL: 'Lake Paho Conservation Area - B Campground' at about 40.4069,-93.6576 (centre of its spurs), 1.40 km from C's site centre, on its own road and entrance off Rt 145. near.py finds no existing entry within ~1 km of that point (the only entry within 3 km is 13793 itself, 1.41 km). Same agency groups (free, FCFS, no hookups, 14 nights). Its spurs sit among trees with woods between them and both shores (water ~65 m+ through woods on imagery) - not waterfront on present evidence.

WATERFRONT (lakeview held for C; lakefront lead): C's gravel pull-offs are on the east side of the lane; the nearest is about 42 m from the east shore across open, unmowed grass with a few trees and a thin bank fringe, the northern ones about 60 m; the west shore is 90 m+ beyond a meadow and tree line. No road lies between the east pull-offs and the water, so the closest pad may meet the open-apron rule, but the pads are faint on leaf-off imagery and couldn't be counted or delimited with confidence, so lakeview stays (lakefront left for AWH or a later look).
PIN: stored 40.41784,-93.66604 = GIS 233, in the grass beside C's lane among the pull-offs; fine (lane centre about 40.4177,-93.6660).
HORSES: brochure 'Horseback riding is permitted only on roads open to vehicles.' No horse camp.
SITES: no site count is published (the brochure caps each site at two camping units); sites.count left unset.
